title: soft-degrade lane allocator with quota preemptive admission
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Implement a lane allocator that performs preemptive quota-aware admission and soft-degrades lower-priority lanes when capacity or credits are constrained. This ticket covers the admission control component, late-binding model-variant selection at admission time, and a soft-eviction mechanism to reclaim resources from free/paid lanes for enterprise traffic when configured by policy. The feature should be pluggable via runtime flags and integrated with metrics for safe rollout.

Why: Current tier routing admits requests greedily into queues and only reacts when requests hit hard quota limits or rejection points. This leads to higher tail latency for high-value customers during transient spikes and suboptimal utilization of cached KV state and batching opportunities. A preemptive, resource-aware admission step lets us favor enterprise/committed requests while still delivering graceful results for free users (e.g., downgraded model variant or queued retry).

Scope: admission controller, lane scoring function, soft-eviction protocol, late-binding model selector for fallback variants, telemetry hooks, config surface in Dedicated and Hosted control planes. Does not include Console UI for policy editing (follow-up PM ticket).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Admission controller enforces per-tenant and per-tier soft budgets and exposes metrics for admitted/evicted/downgraded counts. 2) Under controlled overload tests, enterprise requests maintain configured latency SLOs with >=90% success while free requests receive documented degradations (degraded model variant or queued delay). 3) Late-binding model selection returns a compatible fallback variant when the preferred variant is unavailable due to capacity/quantization constraints. 4) No data plane regressions in request correctness; end-to-end tests pass. 5) Feature gated and toggled via runtime flag for safe canary rollouts.
design_decisions:
- Use a centralized admission controller per region that subscribes to token credit meters and GPU slot utilization.
- Scoring: (tier_weight * queue_priority) - (estimated_cost * age_factor). We chose a soft-degrade (signal + graceful eviction) rather than hard-preempt to avoid user-visible errors.
- Late-binding: select fallback model variant only when admission indicates the original variant would exceed the immediate capacity window; fallback table defined by model-compatibility matrix.
- Metrics: emit admission_decision, evicted_request, downgraded_request, fallback_selected labels.
- Persist minimal eviction metadata to allow request replay within a short TTL instead of dropping entirely.
implementation_notes:
Plan: 1) Add admission controller service with gRPC API for enqueue/admit/evict decisions. 2) Integrate with existing credit buckets (credit-service) via pull model and augment with regional GPU utilization stream. 3) Implement lane allocator library used by runtime to make decisions with policy config. 4) Wire late-binding selector into request lifecycle after admission but before scheduling onto GPU. 5) Add unit and integration tests with synthetic load harness (see test matrix).

Prototype results: local bench using 2-node sim produced ~25% fewer hard rejects and improved 95th latency for enterprise by 18% when soft-eviction enabled. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5128 (draft).
rollout_plan:
Phase 0: feature flag off in prod; deploy admission controller in canary region (us-west-2) behind flag. Phase 1: enable admission decisions for 5% of traffic for non-production tenants and observe metrics for 48h. Phase 2: enable for paid and enterprise only at 20% traffic; monitor latency SLOs and evictions. Phase 3: enable for all tiers with fallback-to-variant policy enabled for free tier. Rollback: Flip flag, admission controller returns 'pass-through' decisions.

Canary metrics: enterprise 95th latency, free-tier successful response rate, evicted_request rate, fallback_success rate, overall GPU utilization.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring and eviction logic. Integration test: simulated mixed-tier workload driver that asserts enterprise latency remains within SLO under burst loads. Chaos test: restart admission controller and ensure clients fail-open to pass-through mode. Regression: run existing end-to-end suite for generation, embeddings, and chat to ensure no functional drift. Load test script: scripts/load/eviction_harness.py (link in docs).
